yearPlan.notice: Generated by scripts/compile-year-plan.mjs; edit the source planning documents, then npm run records. Allocations are proposals, not mastery.

chapters.title: 1. I can belong and contribute
chapters.journey: Arrival, invitation and a supported first responsibility at Sunday Markets.
chapters.carry: Knows how to act, seek help and resume; provisional aspiration, first useful contribution.

chapters.title: 2. I can choose an opportunity
chapters.journey: Meets advice/support, compares futures and crosses a threshold through an application.
chapters.carry: Source judgement and a reasoned application; a fictional role and commitments.

chapters.title: 3. My plans can change
chapters.journey: Encounters external change; investigates and adapts without being blamed for circumstances.
chapters.carry: Better alternatives, decision model and revised fictional budget.

chapters.title: 4. We can make work better
chapters.journey: Learns with others, takes initiative and contributes to a shared decision.
chapters.carry: Communication and collaboration evidence; a justified community proposal.

chapters.title: 5. I can show what I know
chapters.journey: Pauses, consolidates and demonstrates readiness; no manufactured story crisis for revision.
chapters.carry: Feedback, catch-up and a secure Unit 3 foundation.

chapters.title: 6. I can participate responsibly
chapters.journey: New role, interview, workplace expectations, rights and culture broaden the first idea of success.
chapters.carry: Observed communication, source-grounded conditions, values comparison and a small learning plan.

chapters.title: 7. I can respond and renew
chapters.journey: Handles feedback and concerns, seeks support, learns and applies something new.
chapters.carry: Improvement/recovery plan, justified advice pathway, completed CPD cycle.

chapters.title: 8. I can choose my next direction
chapters.journey: Return with learning: explains changed aspirations and applies capability elsewhere.
chapters.carry: Selected evidence and a provisional future; plural success, not a wealth ranking.

world.title: Environment and buildings
world.role: A community with homes, employers and services. Home Base supports planning; a Jobs Centre/advice service supports research, applications and later transitions; community services support shared decisions. No Megatrends or Initiative building is required. Exact service integration remains to design.

world.title: Avatar Studio and identity
world.role: Optional personalisation or ready-made avatar; provisional aspirations can change. Appearance and gaming skill do not determine learning access or achievement.

world.title: Earnings, saving and shop
world.role: First pay makes choice visible; later fictional budgets create trade-offs. Essential support is free. Money, purchases and badges are engagement/progression signals, not marks.

world.title: Community and tax
world.role: Simulated earnings can help explain shared services; formal class-investment work comes later. No universal rate, treasury integration or automatic promotion is locked. A teacher-held fictional fund is enough for planning.

world.title: Global possibilities
world.role: Wider labour-market comparisons are curriculum in Unit 3. Global multiplayer, trade and cross-school identity remain deferred; these are different meanings of “global”.

world.title: Disrepair → Growth → Flourishing
world.role: Environmental development can show shared change. It is not the hero cycle, individual capability scale or a fixed calendar of earned upgrades. No week below forces a world-stage switch.

weeks.focus: CE-EXP-V2-00 plus existing **Live Music & Sunday Markets**. Understand the world through one useful, manageable role. Separate short digital-safety preparation from the market.
weeks.objectives: Operational: locate role/help, make a change, recognise an effect, leave/resume. Market: optional I/P examples for U3-EB-01–03, not coverage. Separate T/P: U3-ES-DIG-02; I: U3-ES-COM-04.

weeks.evidence: Can explain the role and effect with support; observe adult-rescue points. Interest and usability separate from learning. Safety case: identify risk and safer action.
weeks.gaps: Reuse latest Sunday Markets/guided choices and 00/06; no independent-writing claim. Do not consume the whole week with cosmetics or require a badge as mastery. Market remains the next detailed pilot after review.

weeks.objectives: T/P/A: U3-LWE-01–03; U3-ES-DIG-01, U3-ES-CRIT-01–03. T/P: U3-ES-PROB-01–02, U3-ES-TIME-01. Compare growth and jobs across locations; distinguish evidence from assertion and bias.

weeks.evidence: Compare credible/current sources, include all labour-market categories and explain limitations; generate own questions/options. Teacher checks reasoning.
weeks.gaps: Reuse 02 and relevant Financing My Future research. Labour-market facts need current sources at authoring. New practice for questioning is a proposed addition to 02, not a changed canonical mapping.

weeks.focus: **01: The opportunity I might miss**, with **06: A public profile causes a problem**. Seek work and communicate suitability.
weeks.objectives: T/P/A, As?: U3-CB-01–06; U3-ES-COM-01–02, U3-ES-DIG-03–04, U3-ES-TIME-01. R/A: U3-ES-DIG-02, U3-ES-CRIT-03. Cover online/written/verbal routes and SAO/STAR/CAR.
weeks.mode: Teach/worked examples + Dedicated documents + Observed verbal response; service return to world.
weeks.evidence: Ad requirements matched to a relevant cover letter and structured response; changed-ad check tests adaptation. Practise electronic communication using approved/mock systems.
weeks.gaps: Reuse 01/06, CE-PILOT-01 teaching pattern and school Task 5 components; verify all techniques, not SAO alone. Résumé only as required/contextually useful. Two weeks is tight; feedback continues in consolidation. Formal Unit 4 interview process stays later.

weeks.focus: **03: The town changes overnight** with **05: My plan no longer adds up**. A changed work situation makes sources, risk and finance matter.
weeks.objectives: T/P/A, As?: U3-NOW-01–03; U3-PM-01–05; U3-ES-PROB-01–03. T/P: U3-ES-TIME-03; P: U3-ES-DIG-04; R/A: U3-LWE-01–03, U3-ES-CRIT-01–03, U3-ES-TIME-01.
weeks.mode: Bounded world change → Teach + Dedicated source/case comparison and spreadsheet budget; supported options.
weeks.evidence: Explain trend → work impact; independently generate alternatives; use and evaluate a decision model; revise a fictional budget with contingency and help pathway.
weeks.gaps: Reuse 03/05 and Financing My Future. One scenario cannot teach four megatrends, all life events, risks and six finance strategies: add concise comparison cases/teaching. No real family finance/health data. This is the highest Unit 3 content load.

weeks.focus: **04: Our team is about to let someone down**. Move from supported first contribution to purposeful teamwork, initiative and inclusion.
weeks.mode: Teach + Observed team task with individual roles; World consequence or equivalent case.
weeks.evidence: Each learner contributes reliably, listens/checks meaning and considers others; explain all initiative benefits and an inclusive response. Teacher sees body language/tone, not just selected dialogue.
weeks.gaps: Reuse 04, market Initiative reference/2C where suitable. Market badge does not close these points. Short individual alternatives plus planned interaction for missed observations; no popularity score.

weeks.focus: **07: What should our town fund?** Compact synthesis of already taught learning, not a new project course.
weeks.objectives: A/R: U3-ES-TEAM-04, U3-ES-DIG-04, U3-ES-CRIT-02, U3-ES-PROB-03, U3-PM-05. R/P: U3-ES-COM-01–04.

weeks.evidence: Justify cost/access/work trade-offs; explain how others' evidence affected the decision. Assess reasoning separately from the winning vote.
weeks.gaps: Reuse 07; all listed points taught before this row. No functioning treasury, voting backend or built upgrade required. If compressed, fold the synthesis into 04/05 rather than use the protected reserve.

weeks.focus: Consolidation, absence recovery, feedback, Unit 3 response practice and EST preparation/administration at the actual school window. No new mandatory story arc.

weeks.focus: **09: Feedback I did not want to hear**. Make improvement possible; choose a resilience model and begin a review cycle.

weeks.focus: **12, second pass: seek advice and act**. Transfer the earlier rights knowledge to a different concern and appropriate process.

weeks.focus: **10: The next opportunity needs something new**, with **09** follow-up. Complete the learning begun after interviews; apply and share it.
weeks.objectives: T/P/A: U4-LWE-01–03, U4-ES-DIG-01, U4-ES-CRIT-01–02. R/A: U4-PM-01–03, U4-CB-03–04, U4-ES-TIME-01–03, U4-ES-DIG-03–04. As? investigation if selected in the outline.
weeks.mode: Dedicated small learning opportunity + application in changed case/work task + brief sharing; mentor support.

weeks.focus: **Look back, then look ahead**; existing yearArc payoff, details still to design. Consolidate, recover absences, finish feedback and select evidence of changed capability.

release.purpose: Career Empire is intended as a connected learning system for the whole Careers and Employability curriculum. The Blueprint is currently its game-design document, integrating pedagogy, engagement, educational psychology, curriculum and learning design; it can later become the teacher delivery resource. Connected experiences create reasons to seek knowledge, make choices and learn from consequences; learning outside the 3D world need not become a disconnected subject silo.

productionPlan.now: The connected reader links the year proposal, full curriculum provision and existing experiences. Review the broad sequence and unresolved feasibility before detailing the existing market pilot.

productionPlan.curriculumBoundary: Curriculum drives design from the outset; learner needs shape delivery. Career Empire spans world experiences, dedicated learning, EST revision and teacher-supported work. Exact-point mapping is not proof of teaching, assessment, transfer or formal compliance.
productionPlan.dependencyRule: Keep curriculum, source editions, original experiences and approved decisions intact. Resolve school timing and evidence gaps before claiming delivery feasibility.
productionPlan.deviationRule: Before spending credits or implementing a request outside the active milestone, explain the deviation and ask whether to reprioritise or backlog it. Suggestions are not approvals. Continue Career Empire means read this plan and do only the next approved bounded step.
productionPlan.productionGate: This request authorises Blueprint reader and continuity work. It does not approve the proposed timetable, game expansion, new assets or collection. Retained environment approvals apply only to their original bounded workstreams.

pilot.title: The opportunity I might miss
pilot.position: An example of the learning loop, not the agreed first chapter or week.
pilot.premise: Avery wants a weekend role helping a community venue. The employer cannot see evidence of teamwork in Avery's first response. The opportunity matters, but the character has a supported chance to revise.
pilot.focus: One job-ad requirement and one evidence-based response. This is not a complete application, full selection-criteria unit or summative assessment.
detailFocus: Identify the selected requirement in a job advertisement.
Use STAR (situation, task, action, result) for one response; SAO and CAR remain for later teaching.
Communicate relevant evidence to the intended employer.
pilot.choices: Choose between two fictional roles with the same learning demand, then choose a truthful example from school, home, volunteering or a supplied fictional case. Paid-work experience is not required.
pilot.safeStakes: The first response is returned for clarification. No real countdown, public failure ranking, permanent career lockout or loss of friendship/health points. Pause and retry remain possible.
pilot.fun: A role the player actually wants, a character who responds to their choices, visible improvement after a retry and a small optional original noticeboard joke. The appeal is agency and discovery, not a quiz with decorative travel.

beats.title: Something I want
beats.player: Choose a role and notice the opportunity it could open for Avery.
beats.teacher: Introduce the fictional setting and confirm the shared learning focus; offer a ready-made character.
beats.evidence: The chosen role and a short reason. Engagement information only.

beats.title: My first response is not enough
beats.player: Inspect the ad and try a short response. The employer asks: 'What did you actually do?'
beats.teacher: Observe what students notice before instruction. Do not grade the first attempt as a penalty.
beats.evidence: Save the first attempt and the requirement the student selected.

beats.title: Now I need the technique
beats.player: Compare a vague claim with a specific example; learn STAR and identify its four parts.
beats.teacher: Give explicit instruction, model one response and check understanding. Supply text and spoken alternatives.
beats.evidence: A brief practice response and feedback identifying the next improvement.

beats.title: Make a stronger case
beats.player: Write or dictate a new response, select relevant evidence and explain why it fits the requirement.
beats.teacher: Check relevance, the student's own contribution and the stated outcome. A sentence frame supports students who need it.
beats.evidence: Revised response, matched requirement and short explanation of the change.

beats.title: See what changed, then recover
beats.player: Receive a specific acknowledgement or a clear next revision. Revise without losing access to the opportunity.
beats.teacher: Review the response as meets / developing / needs support. Any future automatic checks assist, not replace, teacher judgement.
beats.evidence: Teacher review, feedback and any retry. Story acknowledgement is provisional, not an automatic cash award.

beats.title: Could I do this somewhere else?
beats.player: Match the approach to a different fictional ad and name one strategy worth keeping.
beats.teacher: Check transfer and ask whether the player cared about improving. Note confusion, friction and support needed.
beats.evidence: Exit response and a separate engagement observation. This does not establish whole-unit mastery.

proof.check: The response addresses the chosen requirement, identifies the student's action and gives a relevant outcome.
proof.method: Compare first and revised responses using a teacher-agreed rubric; include a different-ad exit check.
proof.threshold: Tania must set the pilot success threshold before classroom testing.

proof.check: The player can explain what they wanted, chooses to improve after feedback and notices a consequence.
proof.method: Observe voluntary revision, confusion and off-task friction; ask a short private reflection. Time on screen alone is not success.
proof.threshold: Agree observation criteria with Tania; no arbitrary retention target is claimed.

proof.check: The same learning can be completed without 3D navigation, paid-work history or timed pressure.
proof.method: Test keyboard, reduced motion, text alternative, pause/resume and absence/catch-up on target school devices.
proof.threshold: No learner is blocked from the required learning; unresolved access failures block release.

proof.check: Attempts, review and progress belong to the right student and class and survive resume.
proof.method: Test save/reload, identity, permissions, teacher review and repeat submissions with fictional accounts.
proof.threshold: No lost evidence, cross-student exposure or duplicate reward transaction in the agreed checks.

sessionStart: Read README, current-state, operations and AGENTS.md.
Verify source checkout/revision, public revision and open changes; do not assume parity.
Read applicable decisions and source evidence; separate user approval from assistant reports.
Name bounded scope, owner, dependencies, acceptance checks and record the discussion before work.
Identify change type(s), before/after, affected record IDs and the required surface checklist before editing.

Screen every change against all ST4S triggers in data/st4s-readiness.json; answer its data/location/access/provider/lifecycle/security/safety/tier/evidence questions and record securityPrivacyImpact before implementation.

Primary school-assessment route is the WA Department questionnaire under record73; CEWA is deferred. Read wa-assessment-route.md and wa-assessment-readiness.json. Reuse ST4S controls, but do not require national submission or equate ST4S report conversion with unconditional school approval.
sessionClose: Append material-change record; preserve the superseded record and rationale.
Update current state, work queue, affected design/asset records, discussion log and AGENTS.md.
Regenerate exports; validate record completeness, links, baseline decisions, type/build and focused checks.
Record source, saved version, deployment, live parity, testing and Tania acceptance separately.
If blocked, provide exact patch/base hashes and resume steps; do not create another master.
Resolve and verify every affected surface; keep incomplete integrations visible. Run change:release for the declared scope; hashes alone do not prove reader-facing currency.

Revalidate affected ST4S controls/evidence against exact source/configuration; invalidate stale proof, update retrospective backlog and derived readiness, AGENTS and handoff. Record school release gate separately from Blueprint publication.

Update verified WA answers/evidence, Department decision and school permission, source/configuration scope and critical remediation. Submission, assessment outcome and permission to use real student data remain distinct.
definitionOfDone: Approved scope or explicitly labelled proposal; evidence linked.
Implementation, deployment, testing and Tania acceptance individually recorded.
Blueprint registers/current summary/next action and AGENTS.md updated.
Generated views current; relevant checks pass or named limitations block readiness claims.
Publication verified or explicitly blocked with integration package and successor steps.
Every required change-impact target is updated or specifically checked unchanged with evidence; no pending/blocked target may be called fully integrated.

A feature is not production-complete until its ST4S impact review, applicable controls, implementation checks, tests and current evidence are complete. LIKELY PASS and UNVERIFIED never count as PASS. N-A needs documented reviewed evidence. Never infer compliance from a vendor name.

For WA-first deployment, complete applicable shared security/privacy controls plus actual WA Department and school conditions; do not require full optional ST4S assessment solely to prepare a WA pack. Verified No/gap answers are not compliant controls. Real-data pilots need verified safety, completed treatments and the relevant sector/school permission.
retainedPrinciples: Learning is experienced, not merely tested.
The Career Learning Cycle drives the experience.
The player builds a life, not selects one fixed future.
Choices produce visible and meaningful consequences.
Growth changes both the learner and the world.
Career plans are provisional and adaptability is normal.
Success is broader than income, grades or occupational prestige.
Failure creates learning and recovery, not humiliation or permanent exclusion.
Every curriculum requirement is deliberately mapped and evidenced.
Students receive repeated opportunities to improve and demonstrate achievement.
Individual agency and collective responsibility coexist.
Classroom usability, inclusion and accessibility are design requirements.
The opening shows intriguing possibility, not finished abundance.
Only approved, bounded work moves into production.

st4sReadiness.title: School Deployment, Security, Privacy & ST4S Readiness

governingSource.notes: Guide pp.10–11 readiness list uses parent C/P references, duplicates AI_PR3 and prints AI_5; use detailed AI_T5 and include AI_PR2/AI_SF6A from detailed criteria. No silent omitted control. Question excerpts are locators; full source tier/response columns govern.

statusDefinitions.PASS—VERIFIED: Applicable requirement satisfied for exact scope by current validated evidence; never inferred from provider marketing.
statusDefinitions.LIKELY PASS: Plausible but incomplete proof. Blocks readiness.
statusDefinitions.GAP: Observed missing/unsafe control; source gap may be established while deployed state remains unknown. Blocks readiness.
statusDefinitions.N-A: Documented source-specific non-applicability approved with evidence/date/reviewer. Not a PASS.
statusDefinitions.UNVERIFIED: Unknown configuration, applicability or evidence. Blocks readiness.

tier.candidate: Tier 2 educational game/career guidance only; not a confirmed classification
tier.rationale: P9 data and P10 functionality determine tier. LMS/analytics/two-way communication/payment/file-hosting features may change scope; review full product, not only 3D route.

questions.data: What data is collected or processed, for what purpose, and which fields are personal, sensitive, inferred or optional?
questions.locations: Where are live data, backups, logs, metadata, disaster recovery, test and development data stored AND processed?
questions.accessCountries: Who can access the data, including support, administrators and contractors, and from which countries?
questions.providers: Which third parties/subprocessors receive which data and under which contracts and change-notice terms?
questions.lifecycle: What are retention periods, deletion propagation (including backups), export and termination procedures?
questions.encryption: What encryption and key-management settings protect each transport hop and stored copy?
questions.logging: What is logged, redacted, retained and auditable; who can read/export logs and respond to alerts?
questions.identity: What authentication, MFA, RBAC, session/revocation, password and recovery controls are enforced server-side?
questions.isolation: How is school/class/student isolation enforced and negatively tested against identifier/role tampering?
questions.privacySafety: What privacy, consent, accessibility and student-safety implications, threats and mitigations change?
questions.applicability: Does the ST4S tier, control set, AI module, jurisdiction or conditional evidence applicability change?
questions.verification: Which implementation checks, tests, evidence, policies, diagrams and documentation must be updated?

guardrails: Minimise personal and sensitive data; use synthetic records in development and test. Pseudonyms remain personal when linkable.
Enforce hard school/tenant isolation on the server, database, storage, functions, caches, exports and logs.
Default deny, least privilege and trusted immutable membership; never trust client role, school or student identifiers.
No cross-school discovery by default. Any aggregate comparison needs documented purpose, small-cell protection and security/privacy approval.
Avoid unnecessary student communication/social features; teacher moderation does not replace access control or safety incident handling.
Student-facing AI requires explicit recorded architecture and security approval, privacy/safety assessment, model/provider evidence and AI control applicability review before enablement.
Verify Australian storage AND processing across every component and access country; a database region alone is insufficient.
Never infer compliance from a vendor/product name. Verify deployed configuration, data flows, contracts/subprocessors, operational processes and evidence.

backlog.title: Replace browser-side student authentication and weak password handling
backlog.remediation: Replace client SHA-256 comparison/readable password_hash with server-side managed authentication or a narrowly scoped authenticated session broker. Use a slow salted password KDF if custom auth remains, CSPRNG credentials, rate limits and uniform login errors; revoke direct anonymous credential access. Revoke sessions on reset/deactivation.
backlog.validation: Synthetic student A cannot read any credential hash or impersonate B by altering storage/IDs; brute-force/reset/revocation tests pass.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Make tenant membership trusted and immutable to ordinary users
backlog.remediation: Replace school membership inferred from user-editable teachers.school_id with verified immutable auth-subject membership approved by a school administrator. Lock membership/role columns; enforce tenant-consistent foreign keys and class assignment, and eliminate prototype permissive policies.
backlog.validation: Two synthetic schools; attempted self-reassignment, foreign student/class IDs, revoked staff, RPC and direct REST all denied.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Isolate feedback and moderation data
backlog.remediation: Replace feedback school IDs embedded in untrusted message JSON with server-bound non-null tenant columns. Remove null-school visibility to all authenticated teachers; unaffiliated reports go only to restricted triage. Scope reviewer roles and immutable audit logs; limit anonymous submission and sanitise inputs.
backlog.validation: Anonymous submission cannot forge tenant identity; malformed/missing school IDs never broaden read access; raw responses visible only to authorised reviewers.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Disable default cross-school discovery and validate aggregation
backlog.remediation: Disable anonymous Global Index school/class summaries by default. Any approved cross-school comparison must remove class codes, enforce participation/role controls and minimum cohort thresholds; assess re-identification.
backlog.validation: Unauthenticated and school-A accounts cannot enumerate school-B class codes, small cohorts or identifiable records.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Inventory and verify deployed Supabase configuration
backlog.remediation: Obtain read-only project metadata and catalog export; reconcile to source. Inventory all tables/fields/views/materialized views, auth metadata categories, RLS/grants, extensions, triggers/functions, buckets/policies, Edge Functions, webhooks, scheduled jobs, replicas, log drains and backups.
backlog.validation: Signed deployment/schema comparison and component data-flow inventory; no real record dump required.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Primary project identity and ap-southeast-2 region observed live; deeper dashboard stalled. Authenticated Supabase project metadata/region; read-only database catalogs and settings; bucket/function manifests; redacted logs; project membership and support-access attestations; backup/PITR and restore receipts.

backlog.title: Prove residency, support access and provider assurance
backlog.remediation: Record live, backup, log, metadata, DR/test/dev and Edge execution countries; remote support/admin access countries; full chain of subprocessors and relocation-notice lead times. Collect current in-scope IRAP/SOC2 Type II/ISO27001 proof for every component. Where Australian-only requirements cannot be met, restrict/disable the component or obtain a school-approved compliant deployment plan before migration. A second paused project is visible in the same organisation in ap-northeast-1; establish whether it holds related historical data and any migration/deletion obligations without assuming a connection.
backlog.validation: H1/H2 country matrix, H5 enforceable notification workflow, H6 component coverage and school-specific acceptance signed off.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Primary project identity and ap-southeast-2 region observed live; deeper dashboard stalled. Actual project region/settings; signed current DPA/subprocessor list and support access terms; log/backups/CDN/SMTP contracts; H6 reports; school risk report and hosting conditions.

backlog.title: Review auth configuration, MFA and recovery
backlog.remediation: Verify organisation/admin MFA, invitations, trusted teacher onboarding, RBAC, email verification, password policy, reset-token expiry/single use, redirect allowlist, enumeration/rate limits and session lifetime/invalidation. Enforce server-side rather than UI-only school/email checks.
backlog.validation: Synthetic role/recovery matrix and reviewed redacted settings export.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Define retention/deletion/export and test full restoration
backlog.remediation: Replace login deactivation/anonymised login labels as a substitute for full deletion. Define per-category retention and school-record obligations; cover Auth, responses/reviews, storage, logs, local caches, backups and recipients. Implement authorised export/deletion and resurrection controls; test restore including storage objects.
backlog.validation: Isolated synthetic full restore and deletion/export propagation receipts, RPO/RTO and backup-expiry evidence.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Minimise free text, progress profiles and browser persistence
backlog.remediation: Classify student/staff identifiers, responses/feedback and inferred profiles. Treat wellbeing/financial values as simulated only after verifying provenance; free text may contain sensitive disclosures. Remove unnecessary identity duplication, bound offline persistence, isolate users and clear shared-device data on logout.
backlog.validation: Field/purpose inventory plus shared-device logout, retention and cross-account browser tests.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Inventory integrations, downloads, analytics and supply chain
backlog.remediation: Map Supabase, hosting/CDN, SMTP/SSO, external media/docs, telemetry and any export endpoints. Pin/bundle external JavaScript with integrity review (current Supabase loader uses mutable @2 CDN URL); review browser permissions, file MIME/size/malware checks and log redaction.
backlog.validation: Dependency/endpoint inventory, vulnerability scan, permission and download review, no unapproved student-data egress.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Review classroom communication, boards, safety and AI applicability
backlog.remediation: Review student responses, teacher feedback, community votes/boards, leaderboards, reflections and wellbeing-themed mechanics; minimise communication, document moderation/report/escalation and staff-student contact rules. Verify all runtime/backend AI pathways before a reasoned AI N-A; authoring AI and simulated AI-themed gameplay do not alone establish student-facing AI.
backlog.validation: Safety misuse tests, moderation audit trail and signed complete feature/tier/AI applicability review.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Confirm payments and app/extension applicability
backlog.remediation: Verify shop uses only simulated currency and no card/payment processor across all services. Verify whether native/mobile/desktop/extension builds exist and requested permissions. Record reasoned N-A only with evidence.
backlog.validation: Reviewed complete product inventory and synthetic transaction/permission inspection.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Local source available; deployment and authenticated configuration remain unverified.

backlog.title: Assign operational owners and prepare final school/privacy documents
backlog.remediation: Nominate qualified security/privacy and safeguarding owners; finalise privacy/collection notices, terms, incident notification, training/offboarding, BCP/DR and shared patching responsibilities. Obtain WA public-school risk assessment/catalogue entry and school approval/consent/treatments; separately establish CEWA/ECC requirements.
backlog.validation: Authorised final documents, tabletop and training/access review, school-specific written approval.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Organisation identity/ABN, owner nominations, policy approvals, staff-only WA catalogue/risk report and school/sector requirements.

backlog.title: Independent pre-submission assurance
backlog.remediation: Commission scoped vulnerability assessment, independent penetration test, independent privacy/document review, evidence audit and mock Readiness Check of exact candidate. Fix and retest findings; preserve reports and assessor independence.
backlog.validation: All applicable controls verified, no open blocking findings, final evidence current and mock Ready; authorised submission receipt afterward.
backlog.evidenceRequired: Authorised test scope/accounts and independent qualified reviewers; vendor/hosting testing permission as needed.

releaseGates.name: Development
exitCriteria: Scope and threat/data-flow inventory recorded; synthetic data only; owners and remediation backlog assigned.
Impact screening mandatory for every change; no production-complete claim.

releaseGates.name: Vertical Slice
exitCriteria: End-to-end authenticated synthetic teacher/student flow; negative tenant tests and secure recovery; source/configuration bound.
SAST/dependency/secrets checks, privacy notices draft, logging and lifecycle design exercised; no real student data.

releaseGates.name: School Pilot
exitCriteria: All controls applicable to actual pilot scope resolved and verified or approved N-A; no LIKELY PASS/UNVERIFIED/GAP accepted.
Written school approval, required consent/notification, support/incident ownership, tested restoration/deletion and bounded participant plan; independent scan remediated.

releaseGates.name: External School Pilot
exitCriteria: Independent penetration test including multi-school abuse cases, remediation retested; independent privacy review.
Separate school/sector approvals, contracts, verified onboarding/offboarding and per-school consent/treatments; no cross-school discovery by default.

releaseGates.name: ST4S Ready
exitCriteria: Every applicable control and conditional evidence item verified or documented approved N-A; resolve applicability for every row.
Independent evidence audit and mock Readiness Check fully Ready; final authorised English documents name organisation/company number; verify current framework before submission.

releaseGates.name: ST4S Submitted
exitCriteria: All Ready criteria retained for exact submitted product/version; accountable owner authorises truthful submission.
Store dated questionnaire/submission receipt and assessment scope; submitted is not assessed, approved, certified or WA deployment permission.

enforcement.legacyRule: Existing records remain historical; no retroactive passing stamp. Retrospective backlog covers existing features.
enforcement.publicationBoundary: Blueprint governance reporting may be published while product controls are blocked, if disclosed and existing reader gates pass. This never permits school deployment or submission.
enforcement.impactRule: Every new change requires screening of all triggers. Triggered or unknown items require full impact answers, mapped controls/tests/evidence, owner and review. Production-complete requires verified controls and tests; UNVERIFIED/LIKELY PASS never qualify.

experiences.name: Someone I want to become
experiences.hook: Arrive in a town full of unrealised potential and choose a character that feels like yours.
experiences.stakes: Curiosity, identity and belonging; no penalty for skipping cosmetics.
experiences.theory: No curriculum claim for appearance choices.
experiences.action: Personalise an avatar, explore Home Base and choose a provisional aspiration.
experiences.evidence: Usability and engagement observations only, not a curriculum mark.
experiences.recovery: Change your appearance or aspiration later.
experiences.payoff: Identity, ownership and a reason to return.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: The opportunity I might miss
experiences.hook: A job you want is advertised, but your first application does not show why you fit.
experiences.stakes: The character may miss this opportunity without recognising and addressing the requirements.
experiences.theory: Job-ad requirements, response methods, cover-letter purpose and format, SAO / STAR / CAR.
experiences.action: Inspect the ad, compare a weak and strong response, learn the structure, rehearse and submit a revised application.
experiences.evidence: Annotated ad, matched criteria, cover letter and a reasoned structured response. Teacher checks relevance, not just submission.
experiences.recovery: Specific feedback, another attempt and another suitable opening. No permanent career lockout.
experiences.payoff: Greater readiness and possible story opportunity; earnings and item amounts undecided.
experiences.setting: Employer notice / application service; physical building not fixed

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Which future should I trust?
experiences.hook: Two town feeds give incompatible advice about the jobs likely to grow.
experiences.stakes: A decision based on a misleading claim may cost time or narrow the character's options.
experiences.theory: Reliable labour-market information, growth industries, comparison and bias.
experiences.action: Check source, date, place and evidence; compare industries before recommending a pathway.
experiences.evidence: Source comparison and justified recommendation, including limitations. All labour-market subtopics still need detailed task checks.
experiences.recovery: New evidence allows a revised plan; the first guess is not a permanent score.
experiences.payoff: Confidence in judgement and access to more informed options.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: The town changes overnight
experiences.hook: Automation, climate pressure, demographic change or economic shifts alter available work.
experiences.stakes: The character's original plan may no longer be sufficient.
experiences.theory: Megatrends, effects on work, adaptability, risk and decision-making.
experiences.action: Investigate the change, generate alternatives and compare retraining, relocation or a different role. A candidate class-world infrastructure project can reveal how energy or technology changes work; particular jobs and benefits require evidence.
experiences.evidence: Trend-to-impact explanation and a decision model with reasons and a review point.
experiences.recovery: Supported re-planning, not blame for an external shock.
experiences.payoff: New pathways and visible changes to work in the town.
experiences.setting: Events across existing workplaces; no mandatory Megatrends building
experiences.prerequisites: A starter plan and source-checking experience

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Our team is about to let someone down
experiences.hook: A shared task is slipping and one colleague's perspective has been overlooked.
experiences.stakes: A missed promise or poorer outcome affects the fictional team.
experiences.theory: Initiative, teamwork, diversity, active listening, non-verbal communication and time management.
experiences.action: Listen to viewpoints, clarify roles, propose an improvement, agree a plan and complete a contribution.
experiences.evidence: Teacher-observed communication and role performance, plan revisions and a reasoned reflection.
experiences.recovery: Repair the plan and rebuild trust through actions; no public popularity score.
experiences.payoff: Competence, team trust and a possible community contribution.
experiences.setting: Workplace / shared project; scale and location follow the scenario

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: My plan no longer adds up
experiences.hook: Reduced shifts or an unexpected cost puts something the character cares about at risk.
experiences.stakes: A planned purchase or opportunity may be delayed unless the character adapts.
experiences.theory: Financial goals, tracking, budgeting, saving and investing, contingency and seeking assistance; life events and risk.
experiences.action: Inspect a fictional budget, seek instruction, compare options and revise the plan with a contingency.
experiences.evidence: Before/after budget, justified trade-off and support pathway. Fictional figures only; no personal family disclosure.
experiences.recovery: Support, alternative routes and another attempt remain available even at zero funds.
experiences.payoff: Preparedness and control over a revised plan; wealth is not the learning grade.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: A public profile causes a problem
experiences.hook: A fictional profile or suspicious message creates an avoidable obstacle to an opportunity.
experiences.stakes: The character risks sharing information or being misunderstood.
experiences.theory: Online safety, digital footprint, audience and bias.
experiences.action: Audit the fictional profile, identify the risk and revise privacy and communication choices.
experiences.evidence: Risk explanation and safer response. No access to students' real profiles is needed.
experiences.recovery: Correct the record and practise a safer response without humiliation.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: What should our town fund?
experiences.hook: The class treasury cannot afford every proposed improvement.
experiences.stakes: Choosing one upgrade delays another; the town needs reasons, not just votes.
experiences.theory: Consensus, evidence, communication, budgets and decision-making. The tax model is a simplified simulation, not Australian tax advice.
experiences.action: Investigate a shared class-world need; compare fictional project costs, access, benefits, job/skill implications and trade-offs; propose an allocation, explain a class decision and review the outcome. Candidate projects: repair towards flourishing, a cinema or green-energy infrastructure; none is fixed.
experiences.evidence: Proposal, budget and justification. Assess reasoning, not which project wins or who paid most tax.
experiences.recovery: Deferred proposals remain visible; absent students can contribute through an equivalent task.
experiences.payoff: A progressive upgrade in the 3D world shared by one class, potentially creating new or changing work opportunities. Exact projects, funding thresholds and relationship to Disrepair / Growth / Flourishing remain open; personal Home Base purchases are separate.
experiences.prerequisites: First prototype with a labelled simulated class fund; real sharing needs approved identity/class isolation and a teacher-controlled treasury. Cross-school/global use remains deferred under the Department safety-assessment route.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: The interview becomes real
experiences.hook: An attractive next role requires an interview format the character has not used before.
experiences.stakes: Poor preparation may cost an offer, but not the ability to keep learning.
experiences.theory: Interview types and process, preparation, greeting, responses, questions and conclusion.
experiences.action: Compare formats, rehearse with feedback and complete a teacher-observed interview.
experiences.evidence: Preparation, interview performance and reflection. Simulated dialogue alone does not evidence all verbal/non-verbal skills.
experiences.recovery: Targeted feedback and another interview opportunity.
experiences.payoff: Greater capability and a possible role offer.
experiences.setting: Workplace / interview setting; no fixed new building
experiences.prerequisites: Semester 1 application techniques; Unit 4 teaching begins

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Feedback I did not want to hear
experiences.hook: A performance review shows that effort alone has not met the role's expectations.
experiences.stakes: A responsibility or promotion may be delayed until the character responds.
experiences.theory: Handling feedback, resilience models, performance management and career change.
experiences.action: Listen, clarify, process, analyse and form an improvement plan; practise applying a resilience model.
experiences.evidence: Response to feedback, an action plan and review of progress. Not a judgement of personality or mental health.
experiences.recovery: Coaching, adjusted goals and supported re-entry after setbacks.
experiences.payoff: Growth in capability and an informed next step.
experiences.prerequisites: A shared record of fictional role expectations

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: The next opportunity needs something new
experiences.hook: A new role or changed workplace needs a capability the character does not yet have.
experiences.stakes: The opportunity may be out of reach for now; training has time, cost and effort trade-offs.
experiences.theory: Lifelong learning, its career benefits and the continuing professional development cycle.
experiences.action: Identify needs, compare options, plan and undertake learning, reflect, apply and share it.
experiences.evidence: A CPD plan and evidence of learning transfer and sharing. A training purchase alone is not mastery.
experiences.recovery: Affordable alternatives, help and revised timing after setbacks.
experiences.payoff: A wider range of possible futures and useful capability.
experiences.setting: Workplace, mentor, online provider or community; dedicated hub not required
experiences.prerequisites: A meaningful capability gap and accessible learning options

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Two workplaces, two ways of living
experiences.hook: Two plausible workplaces offer different cultures, responsibilities and ways of working.
experiences.stakes: A good salary does not settle whether either role suits the character's priorities.
experiences.theory: Enterprise culture, culture types, successful characteristics and alignment with individual values.
experiences.action: Investigate workplace practices, compare evidence and explain a personally justified choice.
experiences.evidence: Culture comparison and a reasoned recommendation that considers alternatives and bias.
experiences.recovery: Plans can change; no single career, income or lifestyle earns a moral score.
experiences.payoff: Agency, self-knowledge and a chosen direction.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Something at work is not right
experiences.hook: A fictional payslip, unsafe request or unfair treatment raises a concern.
experiences.stakes: Ignoring the issue can leave the character exposed to detriment; seeking advice is a valid action.
experiences.theory: Employment legislation, award conditions, workplace protocols and grievance processes.
experiences.action: Check appropriate current sources, document the issue, compare advice pathways and choose a justified response.
experiences.evidence: Source-grounded case response. Specific law, award rates and advice services require a fresh authoritative check when the task is written.
experiences.recovery: Teacher support, a non-personal alternative case and accessible advice; no forced trauma disclosure.
experiences.payoff: Preparedness to recognise concerns and seek appropriate help.
experiences.setting: Workplace / advice service; formal Unit 4 learning, not a Unit 3 arbitration module
experiences.prerequisites: School-safe scenario review and current official sources

experiences.time: Brief discovery; duration and frequency to test
experiences.participation: Optional; can occur throughout the year
experiences.name: A small surprise worth finding
experiences.hook: A familiar sign, an unexpected detail or a playful action reveals an original inside joke.
experiences.stakes: None; missing it never blocks learning.
experiences.action: Explore, notice a clue or perform an optional action.
experiences.evidence: Observe delight and distraction separately; no assessment claim.
experiences.recovery: No missable essential reward and no compulsory repeated search.
experiences.payoff: Small treasure, cosmetic token or funny world response; exact rewards to approve.
experiences.setting: World details chosen after the story and map are established
experiences.prerequisites: Teacher approval of joke, trigger and original assets

decisions.title: One curriculum, one connected learning management system
decisions.detail: Career Empire is intended to deliver and manage the whole Careers and Employability curriculum through connected modes: the playable world, dedicated learning spaces, existing EST preparation, assessment and teacher support. The Blueprint is intended to become the teacher resource for delivering the year-long program, connecting curriculum, sequence, preparation, facilitation, assessment and support. Curriculum requirements drive the choice of delivery mode. A world event or productive-failure sequence is not mandatory for every activity. Preserve suitable existing EST memory cards and arcade revision before considering replacement. Results and appropriate earnings may connect back to the world, but learning evidence and game rewards remain distinct; integration rules and full LMS capabilities are not claimed implemented.
decisions.source: Tania, 24 September 2026: Career Empire is the learning management system for the whole curriculum; ok to revise the Blueprint on that basis.
decisions.replaces: Clarifies the scope of V2-D01: meaningful encounters remain useful for world experiences, but are not the universal entry for all curriculum provision. Supersedes the earlier integration recommendation to select a world scenario before reviewing existing curriculum provision. Current concerns are design checks, not guiding educational purpose.

decisions.title: First shared 3D avatar visual direction
decisions.detail: Use CE-AVATAR-CONCEPT-001 as the appearance direction for one initial ECC character, retaining the recognisable identity and uniform with cinematic 3D materials and lighting. Prepare the actual model for the existing shared Avatar Studio and world flow before expanding the wardrobe. A generated picture is not a rigged model or tested gameplay. The derived side/back reference, exact crest artwork, modelling route and runtime acceptance remain production checks; no silent age redesign is approved.
decisions.source: Tania, 7 September 2026: "yes!" in response to whether the displayed first ECC concept was the right visual direction before developing the actual model
decisions.replaces: Resolves the first character appearance-direction gate only. Existing Atlas, curriculum and reward decisions remain unchanged.

decisions.title: Use SCSA sample timing as a flexible scaffold
decisions.detail: Compare the sample course-outline week blocks with proposed experiences and actual lesson constraints. Keep official suggested timing distinct from the game sequence; Tania has not yet selected a final order. Her earlier program may help check workload and assessment timing.
decisions.source: Tania, 6 September; SCSA sample course outline for teaching from 2026
decisions.replaces: No fixed teaching sequence is being imposed.

decisions.title: Experience creates the need to learn
decisions.detail: A meaningful encounter comes before explanation, then supported learning, application, consequences and recovery. Detriment may affect the fictional character; the purpose is a reason to learn, not compulsory distress.
decisions.replaces: A01 wording that implied theory must always come first.

decisions.title: One learning map, two directions
decisions.detail: One set of experience-to-curriculum links powers both views. Preserve exact syllabus points, detail bullets, repeat learning and honest gaps. A mapped proposal is not completed teaching.
decisions.source: Tania, 6 September; Curriculum Experience Mapping, 4-5 September
decisions.replaces: V2 initial paraphrased, one-way Unit 3 ledger.

decisions.title: Whole-year vision; staged delivery
decisions.detail: Plan the full Year 12 journey. Unit 3 belongs in Semester 1 and Unit 4 in Semester 2. Design the first complete learning slice before expanding the world.
decisions.source: Tania, 6 September; approved semester boundary retained
decisions.replaces: Unit 4 as an unspecified parking list only.

decisions.title: Tax contributes to the shared town
decisions.detail: Tax from simulated earnings funds class-owned infrastructure and building improvements. The rate, earning sources, spending authorisation and upgrade costs are not locked.
decisions.source: Tania, 6 September; A09; prior EST setting is 10%
decisions.replaces: General community rewards without a visible treasury loop.

decisions.title: How two development layers interact
decisions.detail: Keep town-wide Disrepair / Growth / Flourishing and consider tax-funded upgrades within each stage. Define what advances each layer, whether funds carry over, and how absence and uneven progress are handled. Cinema/nightclub were illustrative examples, not approved venues.
decisions.source: Tania, 6 September: likes both layers, rules undecided

decisions.title: Success, values and rewards
decisions.detail: Several kinds of success are protected. Decide how choices affect finances, relationships, wellbeing, capability and contribution in this Christian-school context. Salary penalties, volunteering benefits and any composite score are not approved.
decisions.source: Tania, 6 September; earlier Atlas inspiration-over-competition principle
decisions.replaces: Do not infer a final reward formula from examples.

decisions.title: Blueprint drives and records every change
decisions.detail: An approved blueprint step authorises a bounded build. After verification, record what changed, evidence, screenshots or an optional clip, limitations and owner acceptance. A successor must be able to continue without relying on Tania's memory.
decisions.replaces: A vision-only page with no implementation ledger.

decisions.title: Visual continuity from selected 2D work
decisions.detail: Retain selected strong 2D artwork as inspiration, with source images, reasons and 3D translation notes. Existing artwork does not automatically become a finished 3D model or a locked building requirement.

decisions.title: Original inside jokes and discovery
decisions.detail: Easter eggs mean subtle surprises found through exploration or actions, with little treasures or rewards. Original themes remain the default. The movie anecdote explains the effect, not permission to copy a franchise.
decisions.source: Tania, 6 September; A15; Atlas CE-DEC-030 retained

decisions.title: Experiences determine the map
decisions.detail: Define what happens to characters, the relevant learning, choices and support first. Derive believable services, zones, routes and asset requirements afterwards. Old building names do not create an automatic construction list.
decisions.replaces: Production asset checklist as a driver of the design.

decisions.title: Four earlier transformation tracks
decisions.detail: Review Green Futures, Digital Access, Fairer Starts and Wider Horizons as optional project themes. The older map tied separate project stages to taxes and votes; it does not establish approval for their return in V2.
decisions.source: Audit Phaser map environment; Megatrends world/world.js, inspected 6 September
decisions.replaces: Assumption that all four tracks must be reinstated.

decisions.title: Lifelong learning without a forced container
decisions.detail: Keep the Unit 4 learning obligations. Review a retraining / CPD experience in context; keep a dedicated campaign or building only if it earns its place in the design.
decisions.replaces: Automatic restoration of the old Lifelong Learning Hub.

decisions.title: Agency, recovery and plural success
decisions.detail: Career Empire is a career/life simulation, not an RPG. Plans are provisional, setbacks recoverable and the dormant town represents potential rather than personal deficiency. Learning and engagement are tested separately.

decisions.title: Class presence is a future requirement
decisions.detail: Same-class presence and visible earned progression were approved as a future direction. Direct chat, trading, rankings and cross-school participation have separate privacy, moderation and design decisions. Do not reopen presence as if never agreed.
decisions.replaces: V2 initial question treating all visibility as unresolved.

decisions.title: Purpose, time and classroom access
decisions.detail: Declare learning versus engagement, required versus optional, expected time, accessible alternatives and pause/resume/catch-up needs. Cosmetics do not manufacture curriculum evidence.
decisions.replaces: Every feature must claim a curriculum point.

learningLoop: Find the next learning need or meaningful challenge
Understand its purpose and choose the appropriate learning mode
Use prior knowledge or an initial attempt where suitable
Review learning, demonstrate transfer where required, and continue
yearArc: Identity and a provisional ambition; curiosity before pressure.
A wanted role gives sources, applications and communication a purpose.
The town changes; plans and teamwork meet believable constraints. Alternate pressure with support and achievable wins.
Use learning to help shape the town. EST Prep stays available as efficient direct practice; its annual CORE slot remains separate.
Interviews, feedback and workplace culture complicate the first idea of success.
Retrain, recognise workplace concerns, seek advice and revise a chosen future.
Reflect on evidence, capability, contribution and changed aspirations. The town is a shared record of progress, not a wealth ranking.

styleGuide.status: Hero environment fidelity standard approved; individual candidate appearance remains separate
styleGuide.title: A believable world, with a sense of possibility
styleGuide.ethos: Career Empire should feel like a place a young person wants to step into: recognisable, welcoming and full of possibility. Its people have warmth and personality; its buildings have substance, purpose and life inside them. Contemporary architecture, rich planting, natural materials and carefully placed technology create an optimistic near-future town. The camera brings us close enough to care. Light invites us towards an opportunity; movement makes a discovery feel earned. The world can struggle, recover and flourish without losing its identity. The ambition is the depth, craft and emotional presence of the supplied ElevenLabs Town Hall films, translated into a coherent, playable 3D world.
styleGuide.translation:
Approved hero/concept artwork is the visual north star for playable Career Empire. Target polished architectural visualisation / stylised realism: warm sandstone, glass, charcoal/blue framing, layered architecture and rooflines, pergolas/shade, rich paving, dense native Australian landscape, rocks, retaining walls and planters, strong warm directional sunlight, believable shadows/AO, environmental depth and purposeful detail.

Aim for roughly 80–90% of perceived hero richness at normal gameplay viewpoints. This is a visual acceptance ambition, not a measured percentage or current achievement. Browser optimisation must not mean simple, flat, minimal or indiscriminately low-poly.

Optimise through LOD, GPU instancing, atlases, compressed meshes/textures, PBR, normal maps, baked AO/lighting where appropriate, occlusion/frustum culling, selective geometry, distant cards/impostors, repeated modules and cheap interior impressions. Select techniques based on measurement; do not add every technique regardless of benefit.

HERO: ECC Campus, Avatar Studio and major destinations receive highest perceived fidelity. SUPPORTING: medium geometry with excellent materials and planting. BACKGROUND: aggressive LOD/impostors/cheap geometry preserving the town aesthetic.

Existing ECC is functional/blockout-quality relative to this new standard, not the final visual benchmark. Preserve recognition, working geometry and routes. Admin, Student Services and Chapel remain one connected destination. Preserve Chapel reflection and its planned wellbeing role without inventing rewards, clinical claims or curriculum triggers.
styleGuide.authority: Tania explicitly approved the governing environment standard on 13 September 2026. This supersedes earlier proposed-only environment wording. Existing character decisions and exact-asset acceptance boundaries remain.

principles.title: Modern by default; distinctive by purpose
principles.body: Use the approved ECC campus and pavilion family: warm limestone/pale brick, navy framing, timber fins, generous glass, verandas and layered native planting. Historic Town Hall art is retained comparison, not the everyday architecture target. Match material quality and human scale without duplicating every roof.

principles.title: Detailed and tactile, not photographically literal
principles.body: Use convincing stone, glass, cloth, timber, water and foliage with softened, deliberately designed forms. Keep contact shadows, consistent scale and readable silhouettes. Avoid low-detail clay placeholders as final art, shiny plastic surfaces, photographic people in a stylised town, and excessive micro-detail that disappears at play distance.

principles.title: Warm people, teen-appropriate presence
principles.body: Characters should convey curiosity, concern, confidence and recovery through expression and body language. Preserve identity from shot to shot and between studio and world. Translate the supplied pose-sheet warmth into natural 3D movement without making every character constantly smile or cheer. Do not silently replace the existing explorer's jacket with a blazer; approve wardrobe by character and context. Broaden representation through approved character designs, not random regeneration.

principles.title: Nature belongs to the town
principles.body: Use layered planting, varied grass, garden edges, water and places to pause. Integrate paths, ramps, crossings and bridges into continuous terrain. Retain the crafted richness of the selected 2D environment references, but remove their isolated tile presentation. A place should look explorable from ground level as well as understandable from above.

principles.title: Light reveals opportunity
principles.body: Use clear daylight for ordinary exploration and warm interiors against cooler exteriors for selected evening scenes. Maintain visible doors, faces and route surfaces. Cyan or teal marks useful technology and interaction; warm light suggests occupancy. Do not make every view dark blue, coat every edge in neon, or let bloom hide architecture. Night scenes are a lighting variant, not the universal palette.

principles.title: Three related visual layers
principles.body: The town is grounded and spacious. Learning tools and displays may use more focused technology effects. Rewards may briefly use stronger green, gold, cyan or violet celebration cues. Keep them recognisably related without putting a glowing reward-frame around the entire world. Colour is accompanied by symbols and readable text; the reward artwork does not determine game economics.

principles.title: The camera brings the player into the experience
principles.body: Use an aerial view to understand the town, then character-relative perspective to approach a place. Keep the destination readable, show a purposeful reaction where useful, and cross a believable threshold into a consistent interior. The supplied clips begin at ground level; the aerial-to-shoulder connection comes from earlier project guidance. Prefer steady movement over whip pans, excessive blur or unexplained cuts. Cinematics need a skip/reduced-motion alternative in the eventual game.

principles.title: Development changes care and activity, not identity
principles.body: Disrepair, Growth and Flourishing should retain the same underlying architecture, route graph and character proportions. Show weathering and reduced activity, then repair, then maintenance and life. A disruption is a separate temporary layer and personal progression is separate again. Do not turn disadvantage into ugliness or make a crisis erase all visual evidence of earned progress.

styleGuide.paletteNote: Proposed working swatches, not sampled values or official ECC brand colours. Material, lighting and skin tones must keep their natural variation. Use the authorised ECC brand source for logos and exact institutional colours; do not infer them from this small contact sheet. Violet belongs mainly to selected interface/reward accents, not a global colour wash.
avoid: Flat isometric cut-outs presented as finished 3D conversion; single textured facades used for unrestricted orbit.
A uniform town of old-fashioned civic buildings, or an equally uniform town of glass boxes.
A constantly dark neon city, permanent portal spectacle, floating holograms without purpose or strong bloom over every edge.
Miniature white display islands, oversized toy proportions, blank interiors, floating feet and doors that cannot be approached.
Uncontrolled changes to faces, hair, uniforms, badges, building footprints, doorway locations or time of day between shots.
Baked-in generated text, invented school crests, copied cultural motifs, arbitrary reward values or new gameplay mechanics hidden inside an art brief.
workflow: Choose a named reference for each job: architecture, character identity, material/lighting and camera. Attach the actual files; filenames in a prompt alone do not give a generator access to them.
Write the asset's purpose and intended experience. Lock identity, silhouette, dimensions/scale, entrance position, materials, lighting and exclusions before requesting variations.

Reuse the approved source set first. Develop the dimensioned approach and modular kit in the separate candidate; additional reference generation or vendor spending requires explicit scope and approval.

Approve one reference set, then build or commission the actual mesh, materials, rig and animation. Reuse the same geometry for states and camera shots; do not generate a different building for every frame.

Compare a rendered film reference with a real-time engine test on target school hardware. Agree measurable asset, lighting and performance budgets before production; no frame-rate or film-quality promise is made by this guide.

Record source, prompt, tool/model/version where available, date, rights, parent references, output, approval status and runtime test evidence. Keep original references and editable source aligned with the live Blueprint record.

prompts.title: Core style block
prompts.text: Career Empire: semi-realistic ECC Career Campus + Campus-to-Career Corridor for a career-and-life simulation. Attach the current CE-CAMPUS-01, CE-CAMPUS-02 and relevant CE-STUDIO-CONCEPT-01 originals; these control architecture and material treatment. Warm limestone/pale brick, navy frames, timber fins, large glass, native planting and shaded walking paths. Restrained teal interaction; warm Western Australian daylight; believable human scale, entrance and ground contact. No toy-like blockouts, constant neon, copied civic monuments, invented logos or literal claims about ECC geography. Preserve selected character identity separately. A concept is not a mesh or finished playable scene. These templates do not authorise new generation or spending.

prompts.title: Selected building to 3D concept
prompts.text: Use the Core style block. SUBJECT: [named building and reference ID]. PURPOSE: [approved experience or reference study]. Reference A controls the selected building's recognisable silhouette, materials and activity; reference B, the approved campus/pavilion concept, controls the shared material and architectural quality. Older Town Hall frames are optional historical camera studies, not current building authority. Reinterpret this design as a complete walkable building at human scale. Keep [roof profile, material accents and distinctive features]. Show [ground-level three-quarter approach / side-rear view / one step inside the entrance] in [clear daylight / agreed evening light]. Keep the entrance usable and visible, integrate continuous ground and planting, and provide credible interior depth. Preserve the same building geometry across the set. [State] changes maintenance and activity, not footprint or doorway location. No detached display base, fake paper cut-out, copied Town Hall columns on every building, or conversion into a different architectural design. This output is concept reference only, not a production model.

prompts.title: Character to cinematic 3D reference
prompts.text: Use the Core style block. CHARACTER: [approved character ID]. Attach the identity reference and outfit reference separately. Preserve the approved face, hair, skin tone, approximate age, body proportions and identity-specific details. Match the warmth and expressive clarity of the supplied character poses while using dimensional facial forms, believable cloth, groomed stylised hair and grounded contact shadows. Keep the result appropriate for a Year 12 audience; do not silently de-age the character. Outfit: [approved outfit], with the exact badge placement and left/right accessories retained. Pose/action: [one natural action]. Camera: [full-body three-quarter reference / shoulder approach / expression close-up]. No face drift, random uniform redesign, mirrored badge/watch or permanently exaggerated grin. A reference image is not a rigged 3D character.

prompts.title: Building-entry video brief
prompts.text: Use the Core style block. Attach the approved character reference, building exterior, matching interior and, only for historical camera comparison, the selected Town Hall clip. No current campus film is supplied or approved by this template. Produce a proposed 8-10 second 16:9 reference film at the tool's supported output settings. Begin behind and slightly to one side of the character, looking towards the readable entrance. Move forward smoothly with grounded footsteps; let the destination fill more of the frame. Include a short, natural reaction only if it serves the moment. Cross the actual doorway into the matching interior without passing through a wall or changing the floor plan. Keep face, hair, outfit, badge, backpack, light direction and architecture consistent. ENTRY EFFECT: [restrained doorway light by default under existing guidance; use a stronger portal only after explicit approval]. If an effect is chosen, keep it local to the doorway and keep interior depth legible. No automatic aerial opening: request that as a separate connecting shot if needed. No teleport cut, sudden day/night swap, fisheye, camera shake, foot sliding, hard strobe, geometry morph, generated captions or invented interface. This is a visual reference; game timing and interaction remain separately designed.

prompts.title: Reward or tool graphic
prompts.text: Use the same Career Empire visual family but the focused interface/celebration layer. PURPOSE: [confirmed feedback state]. Create one clear [symbol or motif] with dimensional material, a restrained luminous edge and a clean silhouette. Use [approved role colour] against [transparent or specified background]. Preserve generous clear space for separately rendered text and values. No words, numbers, school logo or invented reward amount inside the generated image. Stronger glow is allowed locally for this brief celebration, not as the environment's permanent look. Keep the symbol readable without colour alone. Confirm the requested file format and transparency from the output, not from the prompt's promise.

checks: Could this asset and the supplied Town Hall film plausibly belong in the same world?
Does it preserve the selected design while adding credible depth, scale, material and movement?
Is the important action or entrance immediately readable, with the world still visible around it?
Do the character, lighting, doorway and interior stay consistent across views and frames?
Does technology support meaning, with stronger effects reserved for a purpose?
Can the eventual playable version meet access, camera, collision, rig and school-device requirements?
Are reference preference, proposed interpretation, accepted design and tested implementation labelled separately?

Current production: autonomous reversible ECC fidelity pilot, fixed-view comparison and measured optimisation, then progressive rollout by tier. Avatar/wardrobe work remains paused.
Exact measured performance budgets, faithful ECC landmarks and verified branding remain review dependencies, not settled by concept approval.

kinds.title: Decision, approval or veto
kinds.purpose: An approval can affect any domain; explicitly assess all affected domains rather than changing only the decision register.

kinds.title: Curriculum, cohort or assessment
kinds.purpose: Change the learning source and all places that represent its content or timing.

kinds.title: Activity or learning-flow change
kinds.purpose: Change the student's whole experience and its evidence/teacher path, not just an activity description.

kinds.title: Visual direction, image or film
kinds.purpose: An accepted visual change must propagate to the gallery, building/avatar records, hero/poster and production priorities.

kinds.title: Building, layout or environment
kinds.purpose: Reconcile the place's design, visual identity, purpose, routes and production state.

kinds.title: Avatar, clothing or rig
kinds.purpose: Reconcile identity/wardrobe direction, appearance, components, model/testing and every current visual placement.

kinds.title: Gameplay, economy or progression
kinds.purpose: Reconcile mechanics with the experience, rewards, evidence and protected design boundaries.

kinds.title: Implementation or bug fix
kinds.purpose: Record behavior before/after and regression proof; implementation is not approval or deployment.

kinds.title: Release, hosting or recovery
kinds.purpose: Reconcile source, deployed bytes, links/access, representative images and recovery; do not use publication as a proxy for semantic currency.

kinds.title: Research, evidence or terminology
kinds.purpose: Attach evidence to the affected claim and propagate conclusions without converting findings into unapproved decisions.

kinds.title: Workflow, audit or tracking
kinds.purpose: Repair the update mechanism and explicitly report inherited integration gaps instead of claiming the whole Blueprint is current.

kinds.title: School deployment, security, privacy or student safety
kinds.purpose: Apply the ST4S gate to all affected product, provider, data and operational changes.

changeWorkflows.completionRule: Each required surface needs a specific action or reasoned no-change result, source record IDs, owner, acceptance check and evidence. Completed changes need passed source/reader checks for every surface. Blocked or pending surfaces keep the change incomplete. Ready-for-publication is not complete: only publication may remain pending after every other required source/reader target passes. Completion requires the independent live check.
changeWorkflows.limits: These checks enforce impact coverage and evidence/freshness, not the truth of an approval or the quality of a human visual judgement. Missing originals cannot be replaced with guessed images. Unseen chats still require intake.

securityPrivacyGate.rule: Every new change requires screening of all triggers. Triggered or unknown items require full impact answers, mapped controls/tests/evidence, owner and review. Production-complete requires verified controls and tests; UNVERIFIED/LIKELY PASS never qualify.
securityPrivacyGate.historicalBoundary: Existing records remain historical; no retroactive passing stamp. Retrospective backlog covers existing features.
securityPrivacyGate.baseline: WA Department questionnaire v4c under CE-CHANGE-20260917-73; ST4S source register retained as reference/history, not the governing assessment test.

release.scope: Connected Blueprint reader and successor handover, including current canonical planning views; no game release.
release.disclosure: Current reader work does not close older integration tasks. Fresh monitor found 216 pending intake items, 37 incomplete integrations and 12 folders with protection/coverage errors. These are not curriculum gaps or verified product failures. WA readiness remains unverified; ST4S optional. Year allocations remain proposals; successor account access unverified.
